sections.title: Remote server
sections.lede: Where the site lives now. The script logs in over SSH, copies the files with rsync and reaches the database from there.

fields.label: SSH host
fields.help: IP address or hostname you SSH into. For managed hosts (WP Engine, Kinsta, Cloudways…) it is shown in the hosting dashboard under SSH/SFTP access.

fields.label: SSH user
fields.help: The account you log in as. It needs read access to the web root and, for the remote export method, permission to run mysqldump.

fields.label: SSH port
fields.help: 22 unless your host says otherwise. Kinsta and some others use a custom port per site.

fields.label: How do you log in?

options.label: ssh-agent / ~/.ssh/config
options.hint: Keys already loaded in your agent.

fields.help: A private key is the most reliable choice. A password works too but needs the sshpass tool. ssh-agent uses whatever keys you have loaded (ssh-add -l).

fields.label: Private key path
fields.help: Path to the PRIVATE key (not the .pub file). ~ is expanded. The key must not be readable by others: chmod 600 ~/.ssh/your_key.

fields.label: SSH password
fields.help: Sent to sshpass through an environment variable, never on the command line. Install sshpass locally (apt install sshpass / brew install hudochenkov/sshpass/sshpass).

fields.label: Remote web root
fields.help: Absolute path of the site on the server: the folder that contains wp-config.php (WordPress) or artisan (Laravel). Run pwd after SSH-ing in and cd-ing to the site to find it.

fields.label: Remote domain
fields.help: The public domain of the live site, as stored in the database. A scheme or trailing slash is stripped automatically. Every occurrence is replaced with the local domain.

fields.label: Remote scheme
fields.help: Whether the live site uses https. If it differs from the local scheme, URLs are rewritten from one to the other too.

fields.label: Host key checking
fields.help: accept-new stores the server's key the first time and refuses if it ever changes. Needs OpenSSH 7.6 or newer; use yes or no on older clients.

sections.title: Remote database
sections.lede: The live site's database. The host is as seen from the remote server, so 127.0.0.1 means "the same machine as the website".

fields.label: Database name
fields.help: WordPress: DB_NAME in wp-config.php. Laravel: DB_DATABASE in .env.

fields.label: Database user
fields.help: WordPress: DB_USER. Laravel: DB_USERNAME. Needs SELECT, SHOW VIEW and LOCK TABLES (or use a user with read access to everything).

fields.label: Database password
fields.help: WordPress: DB_PASSWORD. Laravel: DB_PASSWORD. Passed through stdin / MYSQL_PWD, never on a command line.

fields.label: Database host (from the server)
fields.help: As seen FROM the remote server. 127.0.0.1 or localhost when the database runs on the same box; otherwise the DB host from wp-config.php / .env (e.g. a managed database hostname).

fields.label: Database port
fields.help: 3306 unless your host uses something else.

fields.label: Export method

options.label: SSH tunnel
options.hint: Your local mysqldump connects through an SSH tunnel. Works when the server has no mysqldump.

options.label: Dump on the server
options.hint: mysqldump runs on the server and streams back gzip-compressed. Usually fastest.

fields.help: tunnel: opens ssh -L to the DB and dumps with your local mysqldump (needs TCP forwarding allowed on the server). remote: runs mysqldump on the server and streams the output back over SSH, no temp files there.

fields.label: Compress the stream
fields.help: Remote method only: gzip the dump on the way. auto uses gzip when both ends have it.

fields.label: Remote client SSL flag
fields.help: Leave empty: the right flag is detected from the client version. Set --skip-ssl (MariaDB client) or --ssl-mode=DISABLED (MySQL client) if you see SSL errors.

fields.label: Extra mysqldump options
fields.help: Appended to every mysqldump call, e.g. --routines --events to include stored procedures and events.

fields.label: Dump file name
fields.help: Optional. Default: dumps/<database>-<timestamp>.sql.

sections.title: Local site
sections.lede: Where the copy goes on this machine and the domain it should answer on.

fields.label: Local web root
fields.help: Absolute path the files are synced into. It is created if missing. The clear-web-root step (opt-in) deletes everything inside it, so never point it at a folder you care about.

fields.label: Local domain
fields.help: The domain your local web server answers on (e.g. example.local, example.test, localhost:8080). It replaces the remote domain everywhere in the database.

fields.label: Local scheme
fields.help: http if your local server has no certificate. When it differs from the remote scheme, https:// URLs are rewritten to http:// (or the other way).

fields.label: Platform
fields.help: auto looks for wp-config.php or artisan locally, then on the server. Pick one if detection guesses wrong; platform-specific steps are skipped otherwise.

fields.label: What to copy
fields.help: full copies the whole web root. code skips the uploads folder (fast refresh of themes/plugins). uploads copies only media.

fields.label: How to copy

options.label: Mirror
options.hint: Also DELETE local files missing remotely

fields.help: sync transfers new and changed files. ignore-existing only adds files you do not have (the original script's behaviour). mirror makes the local folder identical, deleting local extras.

fields.label: Uploads folder
fields.help: Relative to the web root. Default wp-content/uploads (WordPress) or storage/app/public (Laravel).

fields.label: Bandwidth limit (KB/s)
fields.help: Throttle the file transfer so it does not saturate the server or your connection. Empty = no limit.

fields.label: Extra rsync options
fields.help: Appended to the rsync command verbatim.

fields.label: Exclude list file
fields.help: rsync filter rules, one per line. Patterns starting with / are anchored at the web root (e.g. /wp-content/cache/).

sections.title: Local database
sections.lede: The database on this machine that receives the import. Its tables are dropped and replaced (after a backup).

fields.label: Database name
fields.help: Created automatically when missing (see below). Every table in it is dropped and replaced by the remote ones.

fields.label: Database user
fields.help: Needs to create/drop tables, and to create the database if it does not exist.

fields.label: Database password
fields.help: Written to a temporary option file (mode 600) for the duration of the run, never on a command line.

fields.label: Database host
fields.help: 127.0.0.1 for a local server. For Docker use the published host/port (often 127.0.0.1 and a mapped port).

fields.label: Database port
fields.help: 3306 by default; DDEV/Lando/Docker setups often map a different port.

fields.label: Create the database if missing
fields.help: CREATE DATABASE when import_db_name does not exist yet.

fields.label: Back up before replacing
fields.help: Dumps the existing local database to dumps/<db>-backup-<timestamp>.sql.gz before its tables are dropped. Strongly recommended.

fields.label: Keep local data for tables
fields.help: Tables whose LOCAL data survives the import, space or comma separated, wildcards allowed. Example: wp_options keeps your local URLs, active plugins and settings.

fields.label: Fix MySQL 8 collations
fields.help: Maps utf8mb4_0900_* collations when importing a MySQL 8 dump into MariaDB or MySQL 5.7. auto detects the local server.

fields.label: Keep the downloaded dump
fields.help: Leave the remote dump in dumps/ after a successful import.

fields.label: Local client SSL flag
fields.help: Leave empty unless you see SSL errors locally; then --skip-ssl (MariaDB) or --ssl-mode=DISABLED (MySQL).

fields.label: Backup file name
fields.help: Optional. Default dumps/<db>-backup-<timestamp>.sql.gz.

fields.label: Structure-only tables list
fields.help: File listing tables exported WITHOUT data (logs, sessions, action scheduler…). Wildcards allowed.

sections.title: WordPress & Laravel
sections.lede: What happens to the app after the copy: URLs, local-only settings and host leftovers.

fields.label: Also replace www.<remote domain>
fields.help: Replaces both www.example.com and example.com with the local domain.

fields.label: WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE
fields.help: Written to wp-config.php so plugins know this is not production. Empty = leave as is.

fields.label: WP_DEBUG
fields.help: Turn on WordPress debug mode locally.

fields.label: Discourage search engines
fields.help: Sets blog_public=0 so a publicly reachable local copy is not indexed.

fields.label: Remove cache drop-ins
fields.help: Deletes object-cache.php and advanced-cache.php, which usually point at the host's Redis/Memcached.

fields.label: Local admin user
fields.help: Optional. Creates (or resets the password of) an administrator so you can always log in locally.

fields.label: Local admin password
fields.help: Password for the local admin user.

fields.label: Local admin email
fields.help: Default <user>@<local domain>.

fields.label: Extra WP-CLI options
fields.help: Added to every wp call. --skip-plugins --skip-themes helps when a plugin fatals under WP-CLI.

fields.label: Extra domain pairs file
fields.help: "old new" per line, replaced after the main domain (multisite subdomains, CDN hosts).

fields.label: Search-replace skip list
fields.help: Tables skipped by wp search-replace.

fields.label: Host mu-plugins list
fields.help: mu-plugins removed by host-cleanup.

fields.label: Plugins to deactivate
fields.help: Plugin slugs deactivated by local-hardening if installed.

fields.label: WP Engine config patterns
fields.help: Regexes; matching wp-config.php lines are removed when WP Engine markers are found.

fields.label: APP_ENV
fields.help: Written to the local Laravel .env.

fields.label: APP_DEBUG
fields.help: Written to the local Laravel .env.

fields.label: Kinsta MU plugins URL
fields.help: Only used by the opt-in kinsta-plugins step (when the destination is Kinsta).

fields.label: Reinstall Kinsta MU plugins
fields.help: Download them again even if present.

sections.title: Behaviour
sections.lede: How the run behaves and what it checks. The defaults are fine for most sites.

fields.label: Keep going after a failed step
fields.help: Off: the run stops at the first failed step (later steps, including the after-run hook, do not run). On: every step is attempted and the failures are listed at the end.

fields.label: HTTP check in verify
fields.help: curl the local domain at the end and report the status code.

fields.label: wp db check in verify
fields.help: Run a table check after the import (WordPress).

fields.label: Progress bars for the database (pv)
fields.help: Shows a pv progress bar while the database downloads and imports, in terminal runs when pv is installed. Each bar is an extra process: turn this off on hosts with a per-account process limit ("Process count of N exceeded maximum allowed value"). Colours and emoji are not affected.

fields.label: Disk space check before every run
fields.help: Compares the remote site size with free local space before syncing. Slow on big sites; always done by Check everything.

fields.label: Log folder
fields.help: Relative to the script folder. The GUI reads run history from here.

fields.label: Dump folder
fields.help: Where database dumps and local backups go.

before-run.title: Run the before-run hook
before-run.help: Runs your before-run hook first: start Docker, pull the latest code, take a snapshot, notify a channel. Skipped when no hook is set.

clear-web-root.title: Clear local web root
clear-web-root.help: Deletes EVERYTHING inside the local web root before syncing, so no stale local files survive. Opt-in: off unless you enable it. Refuses /, $HOME and top-level folders.

maintenance-on.title: Enable maintenance mode (local site)
maintenance-on.help: Puts the LOCAL site into maintenance mode during the sync (.maintenance file or artisan down). Skipped automatically when the web root was cleared.

sync-files.title: Sync files from remote
sync-files.help: rsync from the remote web root, honouring the exclude list, What to copy and How to copy. Vanished or unreadable files are a warning, not a failure.

migrate-db.title: Migrate database
migrate-db.help: Exports the remote database, backs up the local one, saves any preserved tables, drops every local table and imports. Shows table counts.

app-config.title: Update app config and URLs
app-config.help: WordPress: writes DB_* and WP_HOME/WP_SITEURL and runs wp search-replace (www variant, domain, extra pairs, scheme). Laravel: updates APP_URL, APP_ENV, APP_DEBUG and DB_* in .env.

host-cleanup.title: Remove WP Engine config and host drop-ins
host-cleanup.help: Removes WP Engine lines from wp-config.php (after a backup), host mu-plugins and cache drop-ins.

kinsta-plugins.title: Install Kinsta MU plugins
kinsta-plugins.help: Downloads Kinsta's MU plugins. Opt-in: only when this copy is going TO Kinsta.

local-hardening.title: Apply local WordPress settings
local-hardening.help: WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE, WP_DEBUG, noindex, deactivates host plugins and optionally creates a local admin.

cache-refresh.title: Flush caches and permalinks
cache-refresh.help: Flushes permalinks, object cache and transients (WordPress) or artisan optimize:clear (Laravel).

verify.title: Verify the migrated site
verify.help: Checks the site loads, the home URL uses the local domain, table counts match and the local domain answers over HTTP.

maintenance-off.title: Disable maintenance mode (local site)
maintenance-off.help: Takes the local site out of maintenance mode. Shares its on/off switch with maintenance-on.

after-run.title: Run the after-run hook
after-run.help: Runs your after-run hook last: reindex search, activate dev plugins, open the site, send a notification. Skipped when no hook is set or when an earlier step failed and Keep going is off.

tools.label: Local tools
tools.help: ssh, rsync, mysql, mysqldump, wp/php… whatever the enabled steps need.

local-root.label: Local web root
local-root.help: Exists (or will be created) and is writable.

ssh.label: SSH login
ssh.help: Logs in with the settings above and checks the remote web root exists.

remote-db.label: Remote database
remote-db.help: Connects with the export method you chose (opens the tunnel if needed) and runs SELECT 1.

local-db.label: Local database
local-db.help: Logs in to the local server and checks the database exists or can be created.

disk.label: Disk space
disk.help: Remote site size (du) against free local space. Can take a while on big sites.
